scope: Ottoman completeness audit — MedalBook 97-family crosswalk and formal gap follow-up
classification_repairs: Sebastopol/Sivastopol 1855 is no longer labelled generically identity-unresolved: SALT proves physical gold and bronze-trial objects, but also says the medal was very likely never awarded; it is retained as proposed-or-unissued and excluded from the formal count.
The MedalBook duplicate headings for Acre, Kars, Silistria, Kurdistan, Cami-i Nusret and Donanma are explicitly crosswalked to stable project families instead of being counted twice.
The 1867 Sultan Abdülaziz London visit medal is isolated as a British/City of London commemorative issue in the related appendix, not counted as an Ottoman state award.
Sanay-i Nefise is retained as a period/name issue within OTT-SANAYI rather than inflated into a second family; 1884, the 1888 regulation and the 1889 list date remain to be aligned.
next_action: Search a new bounded specialist-auction or museum unit for the 1905 final Yemen medal and the formal silver Zaptiye Çavuşları medal. Audit early Ottoman honor ornaments (çelenk, sorguç, tuğ and pre-order gifts) as a separate historical-honours boundary, and locate a licensable full image for the related 1867 London visit medal; do not inflate the formal medal/order count with badges, copies, foreign commemoratives or proposed orders.

publish.reason: Ottoman volume remains incomplete because two documented formal families still lack an eligible complete image and four sources remain blocked, including the newly discovered 2025 Kuşoğlu whole-book PDF.
